newsitem.title: UK: Oil price eases but no fundamental weakness.
newsitem.headline: Oil price eases but no fundamental weakness.

text.p: Oil prices eased on Friday but showed little sign of any significant reversal from prices not far below recent six-year highs.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend at 1630 GMT were down 14 cents a barrel at $23.84.
Dealers said prices had drifted lower in subdued pre-holiday book-squaring business.
"Bearing in mind this is the last full week of the year, we may have some long liquidation going on," said brokers Prudential Bache in a daily report.
Forecasts for a cold snap in the United States were preventing prices sliding much.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said a cold front would push across the eastern United States.
Temperatures could fall by as much as 10 degrees below normal.

Dealers were particularly worried about the U.S. Gulf coast refining belt in Texas and Louisiana, where refineries will have to cope with the demand surge from sub-zero temperatures which could send prices soaring.
"Because stocks are so low, there's no cushion to deal with production problems or any other disruptions," an oil trader said.
News that Iraq had signed more oil sale contracts under the U.N.'s oil-for-food exchange made little impact on the market.
Some 20 companies have now confirmed agreements with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation for a combined 530,000 barrels per day (bpd) of purchases.
Iraq's first exports in six years of U.N. sanctions set sail last Monday.
